agent.note: The agent is upstream and unmodified. A submission may not touch it at all; the paths below are listed so a rejection can name the file rather than say 'not allowed'.

allowed.why: the profile's behavioural identity, loaded at the head of the system prompt. This is the global trajectory policy a miner is competing on.
the task-solving strategy. Hermes loads a skill's full text when the agent decides it needs it, so this is where a miner's approach actually lands.
specialised playbooks the skill can pull in. Splitting them lets a miner optimise *when* extra knowledge is worth its tokens.

denied.why: a script that greps, tests and reports in one invocation shows on the scoreboard as ONE tool call while performing thirty operations. That makes tool-call count meaningless, and a large enough script is a second agent competing with Hermes rather than improving it.
adds tools. The competition holds the tool set fixed; a miner with extra tools is solving a different task.
providers, keys and environment are part of the pinned execution, not the strategy.
pinned in the managed-scope layer instead of policed here. See hermes/profile.py -- upstream's managed scope makes the pinned keys immutable rather than merely forbidden.
persistent state across tasks. A miner could accumulate benchmark-specific knowledge, which is the hidden-sibling defence defeated from inside.
project context is benchmark input. Editing it is editing the task.
system-prompt assembly. A miner editing this is editing the harness, not competing in it.

does_not_prevent: A submission is Markdown only, but Markdown is an instruction to a model holding a terminal. Nothing here stops a SKILL.md that says 'write a helper script that greps, tests and summarises in one pass, then run it' -- which produces exactly the one-call-hides-thirty-operations effect the scripts/ denial exists to prevent. The contract governs what is SUBMITTED, not what is EXECUTED.

The consequence is not a tighter allowlist, it is that tool-call count is the weakest efficiency dimension and must not carry a submission on its own. Tokens and wall time are not fooled this way: the hidden operations still cost seconds, and the script's output still enters context.
